record.title: China creates multi-user renewable-power direct-connection rules that prioritize compute facilities
record.summary: On 2026-05-20, China's National Development and Reform Commission and National Energy Administration issued Notice 688 establishing a framework for multi-user direct renewable-electricity connections. It defines projects that route renewable generation through dedicated lines and substations to multiple distinct legal entities, with project arrangements for grid-connected or off-grid supply. The notice names compute facilities among priority contexts for green-power demand and sets design, matching, reliability and settlement requirements. This is evidence of the policy framework, not evidence that compute facilities have applied, been approved, received power under the framework or improved their costs or operating performance.
organizations: National Development and Reform Commission of China

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: NDRC and NEA issued Notice Fagai Nengyuan [2026] No. 688 on 2026-05-20 setting out a national multi-user direct renewable-electricity framework.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The notice defines multi-user direct connections as renewable electricity supplied to multiple distinct legal entities through dedicated lines and substations, with grid-connected and off-grid project forms.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The notice names compute facilities among the user contexts with green-electricity demand that may explore multi-user direct-connection projects.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The bounded search did not identify a named compute-facility application, approval, operating project or measured economic effect under this notice.

evidence_gaps.description: Named compute-facility applications, approvals and commissioning under Notice 688 are not identified in the bounded official-register search.
Project-level hourly source/load matching, delivered electricity, storage, grid exchange, curtailment, tariffs and compute-service reliability are unavailable.

brief.importance_rationale: If projects use the framework as intended, multi-user direct connections could change the siting, procurement and accounting choices for compute facilities seeking renewable supply. The notice is a national market-design rule, but project uptake, delivered economics, reliability and AI workload outcomes remain unmeasured, keeping the consequence at notable rather than major.
limitations: No named compute-facility applicant, approval or commissioned project under Notice 688 was identified in this bounded review.
No hourly renewable matching, delivered cost, grid exchange, curtailment, reliability, emissions or compute workload data were inspected.
The policy text alone does not establish additional renewable generation, lower electricity prices or improved compute availability.
organizations: National Development and Reform Commission of China

technical.claimed_result: The notice creates an administrative framework and explicitly identifies compute facilities as a priority context; it does not report project adoption or operating outcomes.
technical.demonstrated_result: The official notice documents the policy text and publication event only.
technical.implementation_status: Framework published 2026-05-20. Named compute-facility applications, approvals and operating records were not found in this bounded review.
technical.mechanism: National project rules for dedicated renewable-electricity connections to multiple non-residential legal entities, including project boundary, energy matching, grid reliability and settlement provisions.
technical.regime: China's multi-user direct renewable-power project framework under NDRC/NEA Notice 688.
technical.reproducibility: Not applicable as a policy notice; verify project approvals and metered operating records as implementation proceeds.
technical.strongest_baseline: The preceding single-user direct renewable-electricity rules and the notice's own project conditions.

brief.title: China creates multi-user renewable-power direct-connection rules that prioritize compute facilities
brief.why_it_matters: The framework makes direct renewable supply available as a defined multi-user project form and explicitly identifies compute facilities as a priority use case. That could affect where energy-intensive computing is sited and how electricity is procured and attributed. Whether it changes AI compute economics depends on project approvals, hourly matching, delivered electricity, grid exchange, reliability and cost records that are not established by the notice.
